jobs.prompt:
Release train 2, money fixes (owner orders 2026-10-28). Three parts, all in the files listed as outputs.

B1 - one Anthropic day cap. Today tools/spend.mjs LANE_DAILY_DEFAULTS has anthropic dailyUsd 20 while tools/anthropic.mjs has DAY_CAP_USD = 25. Make spend.mjs the single source: export the default lane caps from spend.mjs (anthropic 20, openrouter 5, unchanged) and make anthropic.mjs import its day cap from there (keep the DAY_CAP_USD export name as an alias so callers do not break; its value becomes 20). Keep TOTAL_CAP_USD 500 and JOB_CAP_USD 5 as they are.

B2 - one price table. Today tools/rates.mjs MODEL_RATES has haiku in 1 / out 5 per MTok (that is Haiku 4.5), while tools/anthropic.mjs PRICES has Haiku 5.5 at 0.10 / 0.50 per MTok (0.50 / 2.50 past 100K-token prompts), which is correct. Published first-party rates (USD per million tokens, cached 2026-10-06): Claude Haiku 5.5 in 0.10 out 0.50 (prompts over 100K: in 0.50 out 2.50); Claude Sonnet 5.5 in 2 out 10, cache read 0.20; Claude Opus 5.5 in 4 out 20, cache read 0.20; Claude Fable 5.1 in 10 out 50, cache read 0.25. Cache writes (5-minute) are 1.25x the input rate. Make ONE table the source of truth (put it in tools/rates.mjs, keyed by family: haiku, sonnet, opus, fable; per-MTok in/out/cacheWrite/cacheRead plus longIn/longOut for haiku) and have tools/anthropic.mjs derive its per-token PRICES from it (divide by 1e6; keep the PRICES export shape and the long-prompt behaviour exactly, so anthropic-lane tests keep passing). rates.mjs modelFamily must also recognise fable. Keep the Haiku cache read at 0.1x input (0.01) since no separate rate is published here.

CAP - one spend cap: $5/day total across both Macs, enforced as $2.50 per Mac, Chicago day. In tools/daily-limit.mjs change DEFAULT_DAILY_LIMIT_USD from 5 to 2.5 (it already counts every paid lane together on the Chicago day; keep that) and make sure the default mode is 'stop' (if a default exists elsewhere, it must resolve to stop). The default ceiling (3x usd) must not let spend pass 2.5 when mode is stop; if the ceiling is only used for notify mode, leave it. In tools/budget-set-commands.mjs set DAILY_AGENT_RAISE_ALLOWANCE_USD to 0: an agent may no longer raise the daily limit at all; only the owner can (keep the owner path unchanged), and the refusal message for an agent raise must say the owner decides spend caps.

Tests in NEW tests/train2-money.test.mjs (first import: import './_isolate-config.mjs';): anthropic DAY_CAP_USD equals spend.mjs's anthropic lane default (20); MODEL_RATES haiku in/out are 0.10/0.50 per MTok and anthropic PRICES for haiku equal those divided by 1e6 (and the long-prompt rates); opus/sonnet/fable rows match the numbers above; modelFamily('claude-fable-5-1') is fable; with no config the effective daily limit is 2.5 and mode stop; an agent raise of any amount is refused with the owner message; an owner raise still works. Do not touch any other file. Existing tests in context must keep passing; if one asserts the old $5 default or the old agent allowance, update only that assertion (it is in your outputs) and say so. The daily-limit and budget test files are in your outputs ONLY so you can update assertions that pin the old $5 default or the old $5 agent raise allowance; change nothing else in them. The ignored tests cover spend paths whose behaviour must not change; the coordinator runs the main ones as checks.

RETRY NOTE: attempt 1 did everything above correctly (236 of 237 money-check tests passed); do the same again. Its only failure: tests/api-workers.test.mjs test 'anthropic spend caps: owner-approved day $25, total $500, job $5; day mode stop refuses before send' (line ~17) still asserts DAY_CAP_USD 25 and limits.dayUsd 25 (got 20). That file is now in your outputs ONLY for that one test: change the title to say day $20, the two 25 assertions to 20, and the three spent.today 24.6 values to 19.6 so the refusal/notify cases still sit just under the cap. Change nothing else in that file.
